slides.title: EES is replacing passport stamps at the Schengen border
slides.body: What to know before a short stay in Europe.

slides.title: Every border crossing is recorded digitally
slides.body: EES automatically registers each entry and exit of non-EU nationals on a short stay at the external border. It applies whether or not you need a visa.

slides.title: Fingerprints and a facial image
slides.body: This record will gradually replace passport stamps. Cyprus and Ireland still stamp passports by hand.

slides.title: The official days-left tool has a gap
slides.body: The EU's online tool does not count any stay that began before 10 April 2026. If you had one in the last 180 days, count it yourself.

slides.title: Count all your stays together
slides.body: The travelnow.info calculator counts every trip you enter, whatever its date.

caption:
The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) records every entry and exit of non-EU nationals on a short stay at the Schengen external border. It applies whether or not you need a visa, and it will gradually replace passport stamps.

One detail worth knowing: the EU's official days-left tool does not count stays that began before 10 April 2026. If you had one in the last 180 days, count it too.
